summary:
BeaconCare is a web app for astronaut health and mental-state monitoring on long missions. It turns an astronaut’s vitals, sleep, mood, stress, exercise and cognitive test results into one clear picture. A lighthouse scene shows overall status, and a 3D human body shows exactly which systems are affected.

It addresses the “Human Health in Space” challenge by helping crews notice problems early when ground support is delayed or unavailable. Spaceflight brings known risks: bone and muscle loss, fluid shift, radiation, disrupted sleep, and isolation and stress. These changes are gradual and easy to miss.

It matters because the astronaut may be the first, and for a long time the only, person to see a problem. BeaconCare gives them clear, explainable guidance and tells them when to contact the flight surgeon.
details:
What it does? BeaconCare has five tabs:

Overview:

The lighthouse, with a green, yellow or red lamp, sky and sea that mirror overall health. Underneath is an interactive 3D body where each system is coloured by status. Hover or tap a system for its measurements, and open an investigation from there.

Spaceflight hazards:

The five spaceflight hazards, with exercise countermeasures, animated 2D exercise demonstrations, and a 28-day adherence calendar.

Health history:

Timeline, graphs and an early-risk score with the working shown.

Medical investigation: guided, non-diagnostic questions and possible explanations, with an escalation level.

Mind & focus:

Three one-minute games (vigilance, working memory, impulse control). Results are compared with a reference and combined with mood, stress and sleep into a plain-language Focus and Mental state read-out.

How it works?

Everything is rule-based. Thresholds, formulas and weights are visible in the app and in the code. A single health-assessment engine produces one status per body system and an overall severity. The lighthouse, anatomy, smart-band panel, alerts and investigations all read that same result, so they cannot disagree. Switching scenarios resets stale state. A demo scenario selector (Healthy, Abnormal, Critical) lets judges see the whole app respond.

Benefits and goals:

Early warning before a problem becomes an emergency; clear explanation of why an alert appeared; support for mental as well as physical health; and a tool that works offline, with no data leaving the device.

Tools and technology used:

HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, with no frameworks or build step.

A software-rendered 3D anatomy engine on canvas.

SVG for charts, the lighthouse and exercise animations.

A seeded random generator for repeatable demo data.

localStorage for saved entries.

GitHub Pages for hosting.

No special hardware. The smart-band stream is simulated.

Safety:

BeaconCare does not diagnose or prescribe. Every screen marks demo data as simulated, and any serious finding points to the Crew Medical Officer and flight surgeon
